title: Beta check-in - data residency enforcement (violations + endpoint config)
summary: Customer reported a spike of RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH errors after enabling hosted region pinning (EU-only). Redwood reviewed example request IDs and confirmed most denials were due to clients still calling the US base URL and one workload routing through an older gateway hostname. Redwood clarified correct EU endpoints + SDK region configuration, and discussed expected behavior under pinned routing (no cross-region fallback). Team aligned on success criteria for GA: zero non-user-caused violations over 7 consecutive days, audit events visible in SIEM export, and clear runbook for capacity events/exception requests.
topics: Observed residency violations and error codes (RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH, RESIDENCY_POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED)
Which endpoint/base URL to use for EU-only orgs
SDK region hints vs server-side pinning behavior
Audit events for allow/deny and what fields customer needs
GA success criteria + monitoring during canary
questions: If EU capacity is exhausted, will Redwood ever fail over to US automatically?
Do audit events include the requested region vs evaluated region and the reason string?
Can we keep a single global base URL and rely on headers to route to EU?
What’s the recommended retry behavior when we get a residency denial?
action_items: HelioPay (Jonas): Update all production clients to use the EU base URL and remove hardcoded us-east endpoint references (target: this week).
Redwood (Monica): Send SDK guidance snippet for Typescript + Python showing correct region config and how to surface residency errors in logs.
Redwood (Amara): Pull top 20 violating request IDs from last 24h and confirm whether any are platform-side routing issues vs client misconfig.
Redwood (Liam): Share sample audit event payloads (residency.policy_evaluated + residency.violation) and confirm SIEM export filter settings for HelioPay.
HelioPay (Saskia/Marta): Confirm internal success criteria wording for their compliance memo (7-day clean run) and whether exception process is acceptable.
next_steps: Redwood to email EU endpoint matrix (Hosted + Dedicated) and recommended DNS patterns.
HelioPay to redeploy services with updated base URL and report violation rate 24h after rollout.
Schedule 30-min follow-up next week to review dashboards, audit export, and GA readiness checklist.
transcript:
Fireflies.ai transcription

Meeting header
Title: Beta check-in - data residency enforcement (violations + endpoint config)
Date: 2025-02-12
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees:
- Liam O'Rourke (Redwood Inference)
- Jasmine Liu (Redwood Inference)
- Amara Diallo (Redwood Inference)
- Monica Patel (Redwood Inference)
- Saskia van Dijk (HelioPay)
- Jonas Keller (HelioPay)
- Marta Rossi (HelioPay)

Summary (auto)
- Reviewed increase in residency-related 4xx errors after enabling EU pinning.
- Identified endpoint configuration mismatches as primary cause.
- Clarified behavior: pinned means no cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed.
- Aligned on GA success criteria and evidence needs.


[00:00] Liam O'Rourke: Alright, cool. I think everyone’s on. Uh, thanks for making time. This is our beta check-in on the data residency enforcement feature, specifically the violations you saw yesterday.

[00:10] Saskia van Dijk: Yeah, thanks Liam. We had like… I don’t know, a few hundred errors in a short window and our on-call got paged.

[00:18] Jasmine Liu: Totally fair. We want this to be boring for you, not page-y.

[00:22] Liam O'Rourke: Maybe to set context, we saw your note in the pilot tracker, “RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH spike after enablement.” Jonas, do you want to describe what you were seeing on your side?

[00:34] Jonas Keller: Sure. We enabled the org setting, pinned region EU-West. Immediately our ingestion service started getting 403s. The error code in the body was residency… region mismatch. Some requests were from our batch jobs. We also saw one error that said policy not evaluated, I think.

[00:52] Monica Patel: Yeah, I saw one screenshot you sent. It was something like "RESIDENCY_POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED". We can talk about that one separately.

[01:01] Marta Rossi: And from compliance, we need to understand if any data actually processed outside the EU or if these were blocked.

[01:09] Amara Diallo: Great question. The intended behavior is these are blocked at admission, before model execution. So a mismatch should be a deny, and we emit an audit event.

[01:18] Saskia van Dijk: Ok, but we saw them in our logs as just errors. We don’t have the audit export hooked up yet.

[01:25] Liam O'Rourke: Yup. We’ll get you sample payloads and make sure export is configured. For today, we pulled a few request IDs you included. Amara, do you want to walk through what you found?

[01:37] Amara Diallo: Sure. We looked at five request IDs from 13:40 to 13:55 UTC. All five came in on the US gateway hostname. So the request was physically landing in us-east, but your org policy is pinned eu-west. That’s why the gatekeeper returns RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH.

[01:58] Jonas Keller: Wait, we’re using the “global” base URL. Like api.redwoodinference.com. Isn’t that supposed to route?

[02:06] Amara Diallo: So there’s two concepts. The global hostname can route when policy allows it, but once pinned region is enabled, we don’t do cross-region routing. And the global hostname today is backed by region-specific edges, but the DNS you’re resolving to is currently us-east.

[02:25] Saskia van Dijk: That’s… annoying.

[02:27] Jasmine Liu: Yeah, and it’s why we’ve been telling beta customers to use the region base URL explicitly, like api.eu-west.redwoodinference.com.

[02:36] Monica Patel: In the SDKs, we also support a region hint, but it won’t override pinning in the wrong direction. It’s more like, “don’t even try the wrong place.”

[02:47] Jonas Keller: Okay, so we need to change base URLs across services.

[02:51] Liam O'Rourke: That’s the main fix, yes. There’s also a second thing: we saw one service calling an older hostname, api-us.redwood… something. That might be from an old config map.

[03:03] Jonas Keller: That could be our batch job, it’s like a legacy worker.

[03:07] Saskia van Dijk: And what about that “policy not evaluated” one? That’s the one that scares me because it sounds like enforcement didn’t happen.

[03:15] Amara Diallo: Totally. That one is different. Policy not evaluated happens when the gateway can’t reach the policy evaluator and the fail-closed behavior is enabled. In your org, because you enabled pinning, we’re defaulting to fail closed during beta.

[03:33] Marta Rossi: So it denied because it couldn’t check?

[03:35] Amara Diallo: Exactly. Denied before processing.

[03:39] Saskia van Dijk: So it’s conservative, not permissive.

[03:42] Amara Diallo: Right.

[03:44] Liam O'Rourke: And just to be explicit, for your compliance question: with these errors, no inference was executed and no prompt/completion content should be stored outside the allowed region because it never got past admission.

[03:58] Marta Rossi: Okay. We’ll want that stated in writing somewhere.

[04:02] Jasmine Liu: We can send a short statement for the beta, and once GA the public docs will cover that.

[04:09] Jonas Keller: Can we avoid per-region base URLs? Like keep one URL and pass a header “region: eu”?

[04:16] Monica Patel: We’ve talked about that, but today, the safe setup is explicit region base URL or SDK region setting plus correct URL. A header alone doesn’t solve where the TCP connection lands.

[04:29] Saskia van Dijk: Yeah, makes sense.

[04:31] Liam O'Rourke: Let’s switch to what you need for GA readiness. You mentioned you got paged. Are you monitoring just raw 4xx rate or specifically these codes?

[04:41] Jonas Keller: Our alert was on error rate for that service. We hadn’t whitelisted these new codes.

[04:47] Jasmine Liu: During rollout, you probably want a separate alert: if residency violations are above, say, 0.1% and not explained by deployment.

[04:56] Saskia van Dijk: I’d rather alert on any violations, to be honest.

[04:59] Liam O'Rourke: That’s fair once configs are clean. But early on, while you’re switching endpoints, it might be noisy.

[05:06] Marta Rossi: From my side, I’d like a report that shows “all requests evaluated and allowed in EU” for a time period.

[05:14] Amara Diallo: The audit events can do that. There’s an event for policy evaluated (allow) and an event for violation (deny). We can also provide metrics in console once you have access.

[05:25] Saskia van Dijk: What fields are in the audit event? Like does it show which region it tried, which region it should be?

[05:31] Amara Diallo: Yes. It includes: org_id, project_id, requested_region (if present), ingress_region, evaluated_region, decision allow/deny, policy_mode pinned or allowed-list, and a reason string.

[05:46] Monica Patel: And request_id so you can correlate.

[05:49] Marta Rossi: And retention?

[05:51] Liam O'Rourke: For enterprise, audit logs are retained 365 days in Redwood, and you can export to Splunk/Sentinel, etc.

[05:58] Saskia van Dijk: Okay.

[06:00] Jonas Keller: Back to capacity. If EU is down or capacity exhausted, do you automatically fail over to US?

[06:07] Amara Diallo: With pinned region enabled: no. That’s a core guarantee. We return an error like CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE_IN_REGION, and it stays in-region. There is an exception mechanism if you explicitly allow cross-region fallback, but it requires a setting, and it generates audit events.

[06:26] Saskia van Dijk: That exception, is it per request? Or per org?

[06:30] Liam O'Rourke: Today it’s per org/project policy, not per request, and it’s controlled and time-bound through an exception process. We can share that process. Most customers prefer strict.

[06:42] Marta Rossi: Our preference is strict. But we may need a documented procedure for “what happens in incident.”

[06:49] Jasmine Liu: Yep. We’ll share the runbook summary: what the error looks like, what support does, and the exception workflow if you ever choose it.

[07:00] Jonas Keller: So the main fix is: use EU base URL. Can you give us the exact one?

[07:05] Monica Patel: For Hosted: https://api.eu-west.redwoodinference.com (and the websocket/streaming is the same host). For Dedicated you’ll have a dedicated endpoint, but your pilot is hosted.

[07:17] Jonas Keller: Okay.

[07:18] Saskia van Dijk: But we have like, three microservices and one job. We’ll need to find all the references.

[07:24] Liam O'Rourke: Understood. If you send us the list of service names, we can help spot-check request IDs after you deploy.

[07:32] Jasmine Liu: Also, one practical thing: if you’re using the Typescript SDK, set the region in the client config so if someone later points to the wrong base URL, you fail fast with a better message.

[07:45] Jonas Keller: We are using Typescript, yes.

[07:48] Monica Patel: Great. I’ll send a code snippet. It’s basically `new Redwood({ apiKey, region: "eu-west" })` and you should use the eu-west host.

[07:57] Saskia van Dijk: Does region: eu-west automatically change the host?

[08:01] Monica Patel: In the latest version, it can, but if you override baseURL explicitly, it won’t. So we recommend you do one or the other, not both in conflicting ways.

[08:10] Jonas Keller: Okay, we probably do baseURL via env var.

[08:14] Monica Patel: Then set baseURL to the EU host and keep region for logging/validation.

[08:20] Liam O'Rourke: Can we talk about success criteria? For GA readiness, what does HelioPay need to say “yes, this is good enough”?

[08:29] Marta Rossi: For compliance: we need evidence that requests are processed in EU only, and logs are available. Also, we need the behavior statement about no cross-region processing even during failover.

[08:42] Saskia van Dijk: For engineering: no unexplained violations. If violations happen because we hit the wrong endpoint, fine, but once fixed, it should be zero. And if your policy evaluator is down, we need to know the error behavior and have an SLO around it.

[08:58] Amara Diallo: The policy evaluator has a dedicated SLO; we can share. During beta, we’re still tuning caching and timeouts, but it’s been stable.

[09:08] Jonas Keller: I’d like a dashboard in the console that shows violations by service or by API key.

[09:14] Jasmine Liu: The console UI is coming, but in the meantime we can give you queries via audit export or logs.

[09:22] Liam O'Rourke: Here’s a proposal for success criteria, tell me if this works: after you update endpoints, we observe seven consecutive days with zero residency violations, excluding intentional tests. And we validate audit export into your SIEM with correct fields.

[09:40] Marta Rossi: Seven days sounds reasonable.

[09:42] Saskia van Dijk: Yeah. And if there’s a violation, we need it to be actionable. The error should say which host to call.

[09:49] Monica Patel: The newer error payload includes a remediation hint and docs link. If you saw a generic message, that might be older.

[09:58] Jonas Keller: The message we saw was like, “request routed to region us-east not allowed.” It didn’t say “use this endpoint.”

[10:05] Monica Patel: Got it. That’s exactly what we improved. We’ll make sure you’re seeing the updated message, something like: "Your org is pinned to eu-west. Send requests to api.eu-west…".

[10:18] Amara Diallo: We can also include the pinned region in the response payload.

[10:22] Saskia van Dijk: Cool.

[10:24] (crosstalk)

[10:25] Liam O'Rourke: Sorry, go ahead Marta.

[10:27] Marta Rossi: One more thing. If you deny at admission, what about logs and traces? Are those also in-region?

[10:34] Amara Diallo: Yes, that’s part of the enforcement project. We enforce region for downstream writes: audit logs, traces, analytics pipelines. For denies, we still emit an audit event, but that event is stored in the pinned region’s logging pipeline.

[10:51] Marta Rossi: Perfect.

[10:53] Jonas Keller: So yesterday, those denies were happening in us-east though, because the request landed there. Doesn’t that mean you wrote some metadata there?

[11:02] Amara Diallo: Good catch. The deny decision happens at the gateway in us-east, but the audit event is forwarded to the org’s pinned region store. We avoid writing request payload. We may log minimal operational metadata locally for debugging, but for enterprise we keep it limited. We can confirm exact fields.

[11:21] Saskia van Dijk: Please confirm. That matters.

[11:24] Liam O'Rourke: We’ll follow up with a written clarification and what “minimal operational metadata” means.

[11:30] Jasmine Liu: Also, once you stop calling the US ingress, that edge case goes away.

[11:36] Jonas Keller: Yep.

[11:38] Liam O'Rourke: Let’s do a quick checklist for your deployment. Jonas, what services are calling Redwood?

[11:45] Jonas Keller: “assistant-api” service, “document-worker,” and a nightly “reindex” job. The reindex might be the one with old host.

[11:57] Monica Patel: And are they all in the same Kubernetes cluster?

[12:01] Jonas Keller: Yes, EU cluster. But we had the base URL set globally in Vault, and I think it was still the US one.

[12:10] Monica Patel: Okay.

[12:12] Liam O'Rourke: Great. Action item: update those env vars to EU host. After you redeploy, send me one request ID from each service and we’ll confirm no violations.

[12:25] Saskia van Dijk: Works.

[12:27] Jasmine Liu: On the alerting side, you may want to add a temporary alert suppression while you roll it out.

[12:33] Saskia van Dijk: We can do that for the service.

[12:36] Marta Rossi: And when can we get the audit export sample payloads?

[12:41] Liam O'Rourke: Today. I’ll send within a couple hours.

[12:45] Marta Rossi: Thanks.

[12:47] Jonas Keller: One last question: we also evaluate Bedrock and Azure OpenAI. They have region selection but it’s kind of hand-wavy. We need a strong guarantee. Are you putting it in contract at GA?

[13:00] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, for enterprise we’ll have contract language around region pinning and routing behavior, plus audit logs as evidence. We’ll loop in our legal/privacy folks when you’re ready.

[13:10] Marta Rossi: Good.

[13:12] Liam O'Rourke: Ok, anything else you want to cover today?

[13:15] Saskia van Dijk: Not really. Just, please make the errors better because my team saw “403 forbidden” and assumed security block.

[13:23] Monica Patel: Totally. In addition to the code, we’ll include the error type and a message. And in the SDK, you’ll see it as a typed exception so you can catch it and log the remediation.

[13:36] Jonas Keller: That’d be great.

[13:38] Liam O'Rourke: Cool. Recap: you’ll update base URLs to EU host, we’ll validate request IDs, we’ll send audit payloads and a written note about no processing outside region for denies, and we’ll align on the 7-day clean run for GA readiness.

[13:55] Jasmine Liu: And we’ll schedule a follow-up next week, 30 minutes.

[13:58] Saskia van Dijk: Sounds good.

[14:00] Marta Rossi: Thanks all.

[14:02] Liam O'Rourke: Thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with light scheduling chatter and ends.)
